tagline: Leading provider of analytical instruments and software solutions for laboratory and scientific analysis
hero_kpi_rationale: Recurring revenue and services constitute a key growth pillar, with a 7% increase in 2025 for services and 12% for precision chemistry consumables, reflecting strong customer demand for precision analytical solutions and instrument services.
company_description: Waters Corporation provides analytical workflow solutions in Asia, the Americas, and Europe. The company operates through two segments, Waters and TA. The company designs, manufactures, sells, and services liquid chromatography, as well as mass spectrometry (MS) technology systems and supports products, including chromatography columns, and other consumable products. It also designs, manufactures, sells, and services thermal analysis, rheometry, and calorimetry instruments for use in predicting the suitability and stability of fine chemicals, pharmaceuticals, water, polymers, metals, and viscous liquids for various industrial, consumer goods, and healthcare products, as well as for life science research; and develops and supplies software-based products that interface with its instruments, as well as other manufacturers' instruments. In addition, the company offers MS technology, which is used in drug discovery and development comprising clinical trial testing, the analysis of proteins in disease processes, nutritional safety analysis, and environmental testing. risks.title: Tariffs and Trade Disruptions
risks.summary: U.S. tariffs of 10% and trade retaliation threaten WAT's cost structure and supply chain. The recent Supreme Court decision invalidating certain tariffs creates significant uncertainty regarding refunds and future trade policy.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report with strong language ('could have a significant impact', 'material effect'). New context in 2025-2026 with Supreme Court decision invalidating tariffs, creating uncertainty. Geopolitical category carries heavy weight for multinational manufacturer with US/Ireland/UK/Singapore operations.

risks.title: Concentrated Geographic Exposure in China
risks.summary: WAT has significant China exposure with sales down 10% in 2024 due to government regulations and macroeconomic conditions. Instruments in China fell 15%, reflecting weakened demand.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified mid-report with concrete data (10% China sales decline in 2024, 15% China instruments decline). Moderate language but quantified impact. Stable trend but Chinese regulatory uncertainty context explicitly mentioned.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Sensitive Data Management
risks.summary: WAT maintains a cybersecurity framework overseen by the Board with annual reports to the Audit Committee. The CIO ensures prevention, detection, and incident response. Periodic external assessments are conducted to validate the program.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned early in report (Item 1A) with structured language and detailed governance. Cybersecurity category carries heavy weight. Stable trend with established management framework and experienced CIO (25 years). No major incident reported but continuous monitoring mentioned.

risks.title: Litigation and Commercial Claims
risks.summary: WAT is involved in various ordinary litigation and claims. Management believes the outcomes, individually or collectively, will not be material to the financial position, but acknowledges inherent uncertainties.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned mid-report (Item 3) with mitigating language ('believes any outcome will not be material'). Acknowledgment of uncertainty but current assessment of non-materiality. Stable trend, ordinary course of business risk.

risks.title: Government Policy Changes and Public Contracts
risks.summary: The new U.S. administration has eliminated, reduced, and defunded certain government agencies, canceled or delayed research contracts and grants. These policy changes affect WAT's government and academic customers.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified late in MD&A section with specific language on agency elimination, funding reduction, and contract cancellation. New context in 2026 with new administration. Significant macro weight for company with government and academic customers.

risks.title: Increased Personnel Expenses and Acquisition Integration
risks.summary: Selling and administrative expenses increased 20% in 2025 due to merit salary increases and transaction/integration costs related to the BDS acquisition. These charges reduce operating margin.
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified late in report with quantified data (merit increases, $82 million in transaction/integration costs). Factual language without dramatic intensity. Stable trend but increasing charges in 2025.
